paper_sections.title: Brain activation patterns associated with cue reactivity and craving in abstinent problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls: an fMRI study
Results for performance data and craving ratings
Correlations between BOLD activation, subjective craving, BDI-II and CAARS

description.value: The study compared fMRI cue-reactivity responses to gambling, smoking-related, neutral, and low-level baseline pictures in treatment-seeking problem gamblers, heavy smokers, and healthy controls, and examined associations between cue-related activation and subjective craving.

design.value: An event-related fMRI picture paradigm compared addiction-related cues with neutral pictures across problem gamblers, heavy smokers, healthy controls, and exploratory high- versus low-FTND smoker subgroups.

name.value: South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS)

description.value: A measure of problem gambling severity.

name.value: Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence (FTND)

description.value: An indicator of nicotine dependence severity.

name.value: 8-item gambling urge questionnaire

description.value: An 8-item questionnaire with a range of 1–7 assessing gambling craving.

name.value: 10-item smoking urge questionnaire

description.value: A 10-item questionnaire with a range of 1–7 assessing nicotine craving.

name.value: Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II)

description.value: The severity of depression symptoms was assessed.

name.value: Conners Adult ADHD Rating Scales (CAARS)

description.value: Scores were used to investigate whether co-morbid ADHD correlated with cue-reactivity-related brain activation.

name.value: problem gamblers (PRG)

description.value: Treatment-seeking PRG; 19 participated and 17 constituted the group used for statistical analysis after MRI data could not be completely acquired for two participants.

inclusion_criteria.value: All PRG were abstinent from gambling for at least 1 week.

exclusion_criteria.value: age under 18 years; difficulty reading Dutch; use of psychotropic medication; a lifetime diagnosis of schizophrenia or psychotic episodes; a 12-month diagnosis of manic disorder; current treatment for mental disorders other than those under study; physical conditions known to influence cognition or motor performance; positive urine screen for alcohol, amphetamines, benzodiazepines, opioids or cocaine; consumption of more than 21 units of alcohol per week

recruitment_method.value: The PRG were recruited from two Dutch addiction treatment centers.

diagnostic_instrument.value: section T of the Diagnostic Interview Schedule

clinical_characteristics.value: The PRG reported an average duration of gambling problems of 13 years; mean SOGS score = 9.6 ± 2.6.

medication_status.value: use of psychotropic medication was an exclusion criterion

name.value: heavy smokers (HSM)

description.value: Current smokers who smoked at least 15 cigarettes per day, did not engage in gambling activities more than twice a year, and participated in experimental smoking cessation.

inclusion_criteria.value: smoked at least 15 cigarettes per day
did not engage in gambling activities more than twice a year
had to be overnight smoking abstinent

exclusion_criteria.value: age under 18 years; difficulty reading Dutch; use of psychotropic medication; a lifetime diagnosis of schizophrenia or psychotic episodes; a 12-month diagnosis of manic disorder; current treatment for mental disorders other than those under study; physical conditions known to influence cognition or motor performance; positive urine screen for alcohol, amphetamines, benzodiazepines, opioids or cocaine; consumption of more than 21 units of alcohol per week; anxiety disorders, depression, obsessive–compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder

recruitment_method.value: The HSM ... group were recruited through advertisements in newspapers.

clinical_characteristics.value: The mean FTND score in the HSM group was M = 4.0; SD = 1.5.

medication_status.value: scanned 16–18 hours abstinent from smoking; abstinence was confirmed with a breath carbon monoxide measurement

name.value: healthy controls (HC)

description.value: Non-smoking and non-gambling healthy controls; 19 participated and 17 constituted the group used for statistical analysis after MRI data could not be completely acquired for two participants.

inclusion_criteria.value: did not have a history of problem gambling
did not engage in gambling activities more than twice in the last year

exclusion_criteria.value: age under 18 years; difficulty reading Dutch; use of psychotropic medication; a lifetime diagnosis of schizophrenia or psychotic episodes; a 12-month diagnosis of manic disorder; current treatment for mental disorders other than those under study; physical conditions known to influence cognition or motor performance; positive urine screen for alcohol, amphetamines, benzodiazepines, opioids or cocaine; consumption of more than 21 units of alcohol per week; anxiety disorders, depression, obsessive–compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder

recruitment_method.value: The HSM and the HC group were recruited through advertisements in newspapers.

name.value: HSM subgroup with high FTND scores

description.value: FTND-high group, n = 10, FTND M = 5.4, SD = 0.5, after a median split.

name.value: HSM subgroup with low FTND scores

description.value: FTND-low group, n = 8, FTND M = 2.9, SD = 1.0, after a median split.

task_description.value: A picture two-choice response task in which 30 gambling pictures, 30 smoking-related pictures, 30 neutral pictures and 30 low-level baseline pictures were presented randomly. Each picture was presented for 5 seconds, with a 2.5-second blank screen between pictures.

instructions.value: Participants had to press a response button with their left index finger when a face was present in the picture and had to press a response button with their right index finger when no face was present. Participants were requested to respond within 5 seconds.

stimuli.value: Gambling, smoking-related, neutral and low-level baseline pictures; low-level baseline pictures showed arrows pointing to the left or right.

task_performance_measures.value: mean reaction time to the pictures in each stimulus category
mean number of errors summed across all conditions

task_description.value: Participants filled out gambling and smoking urge questionnaires before and immediately after fMRI scanning.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Philips Intera full-body fMRI scanner equipped with a standard SENSE RF head coil (Quasar gradient system, Philips Medical Systems BV, Eindhoven, the Netherlands)

description.value: T2*-weighted echo planar images sensitive to blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) contrast were acquired during the task, with 35 axial slices, an interslice gap of 0.3 mm, matrix size 64 × 64 mm, and bandwidth 90 kHz, covering the entire brain except for the inferior regions of the cerebellum.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Philips Intera full-body fMRI scanner

description.value: A sagittal T1-weighed structural scan with 170 slices was made in order to co-register it with the fMRI data.
Images were slice-timed, reoriented and realigned to the first volume. T1-coregistered volumes were normalized to an SPM T1-template and spatially smoothed.

software.value: SPM2 (Statistical Parametric Mapping; Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

steps.value: T1-coregistered volumes were normalized to an SPM T1-template using 12 linear parameters and a set of non-linear cosine basis functions
spatial smoothing was performed using an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Delta functions convolved with a synthetic hemodynamic response function were used to model responses to each stimulus type. For each comparison of interest, single-subject contrast images were entered into second-level random effects analyses.
